title: Terraform plan runs on pull_request with cloud secrets and pull-requests:write — exploitable by PRs
problem: terraform-plan.yml triggers on pull_request (line 4) and injects ARM_CLIENT_SECRET, ARM_* and PG_ADMIN_PASSWORD_DEV/PROD into the job env (lines 16-19, 51, 93), runs `terraform plan` (which executes provider code and data sources, e.g. azurerm_client_config), and has pull-requests: write (line 12) to post comments. A PR that modifies infra/ can alter provider/backend config or add a malicious external data source / module source and exfiltrate the injected Azure credentials and DB passwords, or abuse the write token. The plan output (which can contain sensitive attribute diffs) is posted to the PR (lines 56-67, 98-109). continue-on-error on plan (line 54) also means a failing/tampered plan still proceeds to comment.
fix: Gate the credentialed plan behind a protected GitHub environment so secrets aren't exposed to untrusted PRs (forks default to no secrets / require approval). Split into an unprivileged plan that uploads an artifact + a privileged comment job, or use pull_request_target carefully checking out only the base for the privileged step. Avoid posting raw plan output that can include sensitive values. Don't require real PG passwords for plan (use a dummy -var or flag the secret resources).
verification: A PR from a fork cannot access ARM_CLIENT_SECRET (job shows secret unset / environment approval required); plan comment no longer contains sensitive attribute values.

title: Core2 WriteCallback does not bound payload size (CoreInk does)
problem: onWrite only checks val.empty() and never enforces the documented 64-byte maximum. A long write is accepted in full, copied into an Arduino String (heap allocation), persisted to NVS on every write, and fed to centerX() which computes width = len*6*size and can produce a negative/overflowed int16_t cursor X for very long strings (e.g. len*6*6). CoreInk guards this with `if (val.size() == 0 || val.size() > 64) return;`.
fix: Add the same guard as CoreInk at the top of onWrite: if (val.empty() || val.size() > 64) return;
verification: Send a >64 byte write and confirm it is ignored (display unchanged, nothing persisted to NVS).

title: Auto-FREE block re-fires and self-notifies every loop iteration until render debounce clears
problem: The auto-FREE condition checks `gCurrentMsg != "FREE"`, but gCurrentMsg is only updated to FREE after the debounced render at line 358. Between the moment the timeout expires and the moment the debounced render actually runs (up to REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS=1000 ms later, and the render only happens once millis()-gLastRefreshMs>=1000), this block keeps evaluating true on every wake, re-setting gNeedsRedraw=true and calling xTaskNotifyGive(gMainTask) repeatedly. Because it notifies its own task, ulTaskNotifyTake returns immediately, so the loop spins (no light sleep) burning CPU until the debounce window passes. It also redundantly sets gPendingMsg='FREE' many times. Minor energy waste plus a tight self-wake loop.
fix: Guard against re-entry: track a bool gAutoFreeArmed (set when the timeout first fires, cleared when gCurrentMsg becomes FREE or on reconnect), and only enter the block / notify once. Or check gPendingMsg != "FREE" as well as gCurrentMsg before re-arming. Avoid xTaskNotifyGive when the redraw is already pending.
verification: Disconnect the agent, wait past AUTO_FREE_TIMEOUT, and log loop iteration count / measure current during the 5-min-to-render window; confirm the loop is not spinning and current does not spike for ~1 s.

title: onDisconnect restarts advertising without checking return / state; double-start race with loop watchdog
problem: onDisconnect calls NimBLEDevice::getAdvertising()->start() from the BLE host callback, while the loop's advertising watchdog (line 393-397) independently does stop() then start() every 2 min, and onDisconnect also resets nothing about gLastAdvRestart. If a disconnect happens right as the loop watchdog runs, start() can be invoked twice with no error handling. NimBLE start() returns a bool/can fail (e.g. if a connection raced back in); the result is ignored. More importantly, gLastAdvRestart is not reset on disconnect, so the first post-disconnect watchdog stop()/start() can immediately tear down freshly-started advertising. Low-probability but a real reconnection-robustness gap.
fix: Centralize advertising control in the loop: in onDisconnect just set a flag + notify; let the loop (single-threaded) own start/stop and reset gLastAdvRestart=millis() when it (re)starts advertising. Check the bool return of start()/stop() and retry on failure.
verification: Repeatedly connect/disconnect from the agent at the 2-min watchdog boundary; confirm the device always becomes discoverable again (scan with nRF Connect) and reconnects within one advertising window.

title: Core2 never negotiates a long connection interval — radio wakes far more often than needed
problem: Core2 has no NimBLEServerCallbacks and never calls updateConnParams, so the BLE link uses whatever (typically short, e.g. 7.5-30 ms) connection interval the central chooses. Each connection event wakes the radio and CPU. CoreInk explicitly negotiates a 1000 ms interval with slave latency 0 (line 176-181) to minimize radio wakeups. For a status display that updates seconds-apart at most, a sub-second interval is pure waste and compounds the no-sleep problem.
fix: Add a ServerCallbacks::onConnect that calls pServer->updateConnParams(handle, 800, 800, 0, 400) (1 s interval) mirroring CoreInk, and setCallbacks on the server.
verification: After connecting, inspect the negotiated connection interval (nRF Connect shows it, or log connInfo). Confirm it settles near 1000 ms and that updates still arrive promptly.

title: Wildcard event logger writes all payloads at INFO — leaks presence/calendar content (and risks token leak)
problem: `_log_container_event` subscribes to `*` and logs EVERY event payload at INFO (app.py:152-153, 184-187). Payloads include the BLE presence string from live-status (e.g. 'BUSY · Slack' and any server-enriched meeting context), BLE addresses, and error strings. With `configure_logging` at INFO to stderr (logging.py:8-12) — captured under PyInstaller — this writes presence/calendar-derived content to logs. Any future `logger.debug(data)` in `_pair_with_portal` (currently swallowed by `except: pass` at app.py:136) would also expose the pairing token.
fix: Don't log full payloads at INFO. Log topic + a whitelisted/redacted subset, or move the wildcard subscriber to DEBUG. Add a redaction filter scrubbing `token`/`payload`/live-status content before formatting.
verification: Run a presence change and pairing flow at INFO; grep the log output for the token value and the busy payload string — both must be absent.

title: API base URL is config-overridable with no https/scheme validation; token sent to whatever host is set
problem: `ApiSettings.url` defaults to https (config.py:44) but is freely overridable from on-disk config and used for the BLE-config fetch and live-status poll. There is no validation that the URL is https, so a tampered config.json could point the agent at an http:// or attacker host and the permanent `x-agent-key` token (header at app.py:43, 104; service.py:104) would be sent in cleartext / to the attacker. No host pinning.
fix: Validate `ApiSettings.url` with pydantic `HttpUrl` and assert https scheme (reject http except an explicit localhost dev flag). Consider certificate pinning for the bumeet.es API connector.
verification: Set `api.url` to http:// in config.json and confirm the agent refuses to start / refuses to send the token. Unit-test the validator rejects non-https.

title: `_pending_send` task mutated from three coroutines without synchronization; write cancelled mid-flight; exceptions never retrieved
problem: `self._pending_send` is read/written by `_heartbeat_loop` (line 98) and `_push_combined_state` (line 150, called from both `_api_poll_loop` and `handle_snapshot`). `_push_combined_state` cancels the in-flight send (line 148-149) and starts a new one; the heartbeat's `if _pending_send and not done(): continue` (line 96) races a concurrent cancel+replace. Cancelling `write_now` mid-write (line 149) can interrupt a GATT write between `_last_payload` assignment and transmission, leaving firmware and state inconsistent. These fire-and-forget tasks never have their exceptions retrieved, so failures surface only as 'Task exception was never retrieved' warnings.
fix: Serialize sends through a single asyncio worker/Queue (or guard `_pending_send` with a Lock) that always writes the latest desired payload. Always `add_done_callback` to log task exceptions. Don't cancel a write in progress; let it finish and enqueue the next state.
verification: Stress test rapidly alternating busy/free while API poll and heartbeat run; assert no 'Task exception was never retrieved' warnings and the final firmware payload equals the last requested state.

title: CMIO camera fallback returns True whenever ANY IOVideoDeviceStream entry exists, not when in use
problem: The fallback at lines 181-189 returns True if `ioreg -c IOVideoDeviceStream` produces any non-empty output. IOVideoDeviceStream entries can exist for enumerated capture devices even with no active capture session on many configs, so this can report the camera permanently 'in use', pinning presence to BUSY and misreporting the user. This runs on every poll for any Mac where the AppleH13CamIn path didn't return True (Intel Macs, USB cameras, and every idle poll on Apple Silicon) — so the false positive is the common path.
fix: Don't treat mere existence as active. Use the CoreMediaIO property kCMIODevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere via ctypes (mirroring the audio approach), or parse a specific streaming/client-count property from ioreg rather than presence of the entry.
verification: On an Intel/USB-camera Mac with camera idle, `_poll_camera()` returns False; open Photo Booth and it returns True.

title: Detection loop on shared executor with ~6s blocking ioreg and no per-iteration exception guard
problem: `start` runs `_take_snapshot` on the default ThreadPoolExecutor (line 211); each snapshot can block ~6s (two `subprocess.run(timeout=3)`, lines 172/187) if ioreg hangs, and the callback `handle_snapshot` is awaited inline (lines 212-214) before the next sleep, so real cadence is `poll_interval + snapshot_time + callback_time`, not the configured 2s — bursty and misleading. Snapshots share the default executor with other run_in_executor work and can pile up. There is no try/except around the snapshot+callback, so any exception kills the entire detection loop permanently.
fix: Wrap the snapshot+callback body in try/except that logs and continues. Use a dedicated single-thread executor for detection so it can't be starved by BLE/API work. Reduce/separate camera cadence (see macos-camera-ioreg-subprocess-battery) and lower ioreg timeouts.
verification: Inject a callback that raises once and assert the loop keeps polling. Measure observed interval under a slow callback and confirm it doesn't drift unboundedly.

title: write_now returns silently on timeout/give-up with no error event — BUSY can fail to show for up to 5 minutes
problem: `write_now` waits for `_connected_event` and on 60s timeout logs a warning and RETURNS (line 138) without emitting BLE_ERROR, so the orchestrator/UI believe the state was pushed. The retry loop (lines 140-154) retries once and on second failure just logs. The desired presence is then only re-attempted on the 5-minute heartbeat, so a user's BUSY can silently fail to display for up to 5 minutes with no surfaced error.
fix: Emit a BLE_ERROR event on all give-up paths so upstream knows the push failed, and schedule a near-term retry instead of waiting for the 5-min heartbeat. Make `_WRITE_WAIT_S` (60s) configurable and consider lowering it.
verification: Drive write_now with a fake client that never connects; assert a BLE_ERROR event is emitted and `_last_payload` reflects only confirmed sends.

title: On Windows no signal handler is installed, so the agent has no clean-shutdown path and leaks BLE/keepalive tasks
problem: Signal handlers are installed via `loop.add_signal_handler` (lines 216-217), wrapped in try/except NotImplementedError (line 218) which just `pass`es — Windows doesn't support add_signal_handler. So on Windows `stop_event` is never set and `await stop_event.wait()` (line 223) blocks forever; Ctrl+C/taskkill can't trigger the graceful `finally` that stops detection, cancels API polling, emits APP_STOPPING, and stops the BLE connection (lines 224-232). Background tasks and the BLE link are left dangling on the common Windows termination paths, risking a stuck peripheral and orphaned keepalive writes.
fix: On Windows install `signal.signal(signal.SIGINT/SIGBREAK, ...)` that does `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(stop_event.set)`, or wrap the await in try/except KeyboardInterrupt that runs the same cleanup. Ensure the `finally` cleanup runs on KeyboardInterrupt.
verification: On Windows send Ctrl+C and confirm APP_STOPPING is emitted and BLE disconnect runs (check logs) before exit.

title: Google 'tokens' event listener registered per sync — EventEmitter leak and stale-client writes
problem: syncEvents registers oauth2Client.on('tokens', ...) on every call (google-calendar.service.ts:108). When existingClient is passed from handleCallback the same OAuth2 client instance accumulates a new listener each sync, and the async handler does an unawaited prisma update inside the emitter callback (an unhandled rejection if it throws). Because the auto-sync loop calls syncEvents repeatedly, this leaks listeners and can fire writes from a client whose integration row was meanwhile updated elsewhere, racing token columns. Also, on the refresh path the refresh_token is never re-persisted (Google sometimes rotates it), only access_token/expiry (lines 110-116).
fix: Register the tokens listener once per freshly-created client (it's fine for the per-call createOAuthClient path, but don't reuse a long-lived client with a fresh listener each time). Wrap the handler body in try/catch. Persist refresh_token when present in the tokens event. Prefer explicitly refreshing and saving tokens before the API loop rather than relying on the emitter side effect.
verification: Run repeated syncs on one integration and assert listenerCount('tokens') stays bounded; force a token refresh and confirm a rotated refresh_token is saved.

title: Reconciling deletes via externalId NOT IN (full list) risks param limits and mass-deletes on partial fetch failure
problem: All calendar syncs delete 'events no longer returned' via deleteMany where externalId NOT IN returnedIds (google-calendar.service.ts:190-198, microsoft:157-162, zoom:144-149, webex:159-164, apple:110-115). Two problems: (1) returnedIds can be large (Google paginates 250 at a time with no cap; thousands of events) and is passed as a single IN list — Postgres has a practical bind-parameter ceiling (~65535) and this also builds a huge query plan; (2) the delete only guards on returnedIds.length > 0, so if a later page fetch throws mid-loop the code never reaches the delete (ok), but for Webex the loop breaks on a non-ok response (webex.service.ts:121-124) yet still proceeds to delete using the PARTIAL returnedIds — silently deleting every event from pages it failed to fetch. A transient 5xx therefore wipes real calendar rows.
fix: Only run the reconciliation delete when the full fetch succeeded (track a fetchComplete flag; for Webex, throw instead of break on !res.ok, or skip the delete on partial fetch). Batch the NOT IN deletes in chunks, or switch to a sync-token/etag delta model, or soft-delete by marking status='cancelled' and filtering it out.
verification: Simulate a 500 on page 2 of Webex/Zoom fetch; confirm previously-synced events are NOT deleted. Sync an account with >5000 events; confirm no parameter-limit error.

title: Message delivery simulated with raw setTimeout — lost on restart, unhandled rejection, overwrites cancellation
problem: create() schedules two unawaited setTimeout callbacks (2s -> status 'sent', 7s -> 'delivered') that do prisma.update with no try/catch (messages.service.ts:23-36). If the process restarts in that window the transitions never happen and the message is stuck 'pending'. If the user cancels the message (cancelMessage sets status='cancelled', line 65-68) before the timers fire, the 7s timer still overwrites it back to 'delivered' — a lost-update race that resurrects a cancelled message. If the row was deleted (account deletion cascade) the update throws an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the worker. This is also a fake delivery pipeline (no real device ACK), so 'delivered' is meaningless.
fix: Replace the setTimeout simulation with a real delivery signal: mark 'delivered' only when the agent ACKs (markDelivered already exists). If a simulated transition is truly desired, gate it on a re-read of current status (skip if 'cancelled'), wrap in try/catch, and use a durable job (BullMQ on the existing ioredis) instead of in-process timers.
verification: Create a message, cancel it within 7s, wait 10s, then GET it — status must remain 'cancelled', not 'delivered'. Restart the API mid-window and confirm no unhandled rejection in logs.

title: Token refresh has a read-modify-write race; concurrent refreshes invalidate each other (Zoom/MS/Teams/Webex)
problem: getValidToken/refreshToken (zoom.service.ts:160-173; same pattern in microsoft:95-106 & 233-243, teams:76-83, webex:175-188) read the row, check expiry, call the provider refresh, then write the new token back — with no locking and no transaction. The 60s auto-sync loop and a concurrent agent presence poll can both detect expiry and refresh the SAME integration in parallel. Providers that rotate/invalidate refresh tokens on use (Zoom rotates refresh tokens; Microsoft can) will have one refresh invalidate the other's refresh_token, after which the loser's stored token is dead and the integration breaks (status flips to errors on next call). There is also no narrow expiry skew buffer, so a token expiring mid-request is used and 401s.
fix: Serialize refresh per integration (Redis lock keyed by integrationId, or a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE transaction) so only one refresh runs; have other callers wait and re-read. Persist any rotated refresh_token. Refresh proactively when tokenExpiresAt is within ~2 min (skew buffer) rather than only after it has passed.
verification: Fire two concurrent syncs on an expired Zoom integration; assert only one refresh request hits Zoom and the integration remains active afterward.

title: Non-null assertions on refreshToken/accessToken throw raw 500s and poison getLiveStatus paths
problem: Refresh/presence paths assume credentials exist: microsoft refreshToken! (microsoft-calendar.service.ts:97, 234), teams refreshToken! (teams.service.ts:77), zoom refreshToken! (zoom.service.ts:162), and accessToken! across services (e.g. microsoft:93, slack:94, teams:74). For a demo integration created via connectDemo (integrations.service.ts:224-235) these are null, and for any expired integration whose refresh_token is null/empty (Slack stores null; Google may lack one), getPresence/syncEvents throws 'Cannot read ... of null' or sends 'Bearer null'. In getLiveStatus these are inside Promise.allSettled so they're swallowed (degrade), but via the direct /integrations/:id/presence and /:id/sync routes they surface as unhandled 500s, and the thrown Error (not an HttpException) leaks a stack/Graph response body to the client.
fix: Guard for missing tokens explicitly and throw a typed HttpException (e.g. BadRequest/Conflict 'integration not connected / needs reauth') and set integration status='error' instead of asserting non-null. Skip presence for demo integrations. Never interpolate a possibly-null token into the Authorization header.
verification: Call GET /integrations/:id/presence on a demo integration and on an expired one with null refreshToken; expect a clean 4xx with a safe message, not a 500 with a stack trace.

title: Provider error responses (incl. tokens/PII) interpolated into thrown Error messages and logged
problem: Multiple services throw Error(`... ${await res.text()}`) with the raw provider response body: MS Graph (microsoft-calendar.service.ts:184, 205, 221, 249, 265), teams (113, 129, 135), zoom (192, 209, 217), webex (202, 218, 226), and OAuth callbacks console.error the whole error (auth.controller.ts:72, 94, etc.). Graph/OAuth error bodies can contain correlation IDs, account identifiers, and in token endpoints sometimes echo request context. Because these Errors aren't HttpExceptions, Nest's default filter returns 500 with the message to the client in some paths, and they're written to logs in full. This leaks third-party error detail and aids attackers probing the OAuth flows.
fix: Log provider error bodies at debug level server-side only, and throw a generic typed HttpException to the client (no upstream body). Add a global exception filter that strips internal messages for 5xx. Never console.error raw error objects in callbacks; log a correlation id.
verification: Trigger a Graph 401 during sync; confirm the HTTP response to the client contains no Graph response body and logs contain it only at debug.

title: PostgreSQL 'keepalive' SELECT 1 does not prevent Azure Burstable auto-stop and risks pool churn
problem: The keepalive (prisma.service.ts:15-21, commit ebdde777) runs SELECT 1 every 20 min to 'prevent Azure Burstable tier auto-pause'. This is based on a wrong premise: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server on Burstable (B1ms) does NOT have a connection-idle auto-pause — it only stops if an operator explicitly enabled scheduled/auto stop, which is a compute-level stop that a SELECT 1 cannot prevent (and if the server is stopped, the query just fails, which the code merely logs at warn). So the hack does not solve the stated P1001 problem. Meanwhile B1ms has very low CPU credits and few connections; an unconditional timer query on every API instance burns credits and, combined with Prisma's default pool plus the per-minute sync loop, can exhaust the small connection budget. The keepalive also keeps the timer running with an unawaited async setInterval callback (acceptable but the failure path is silent).
fix: Remove the keepalive and instead (a) disable scheduled auto-stop on the Flexible Server, or (b) handle cold-start P1001 with a connection retry/backoff on startup and lazy reconnect, and (c) right-size the tier if cold starts are unacceptable. If a heartbeat is genuinely needed, make it conditional, infrequent, and surface failures (don't just warn). Tune Prisma connection_limit for B1ms.
verification: Confirm in Azure that the server has no idle auto-pause and that disabling scheduled stop (or adding startup retry) resolves P1001 without the timer. Monitor B1ms CPU credit consumption with the timer removed.

title: getBusyStatus only matches status='confirmed', silently ignoring 'tentative' and mislabeling sources
problem: getBusyStatus filters status: 'confirmed' (integrations.service.ts:311), but provider events can be 'tentative' (Google) or other statuses; those are dropped, so a user accepted-tentative meeting never shows BUSY. Conversely Slack 'events' (synthetic 5-min windows per DM message, slack.service.ts:106-126) are all written status:'confirmed' and counted as calendar busy, so any recent Slack DM marks the user BUSY on the device for 5 minutes — a false-positive presence signal feeding the e-ink display. The provider->source map (integrations.service.ts:149-155) also has no 'slack'/'apple'/'teams' calendar entries, so those events render with a raw provider string.
fix: Decide which statuses count as busy (include 'tentative' if desired) and filter accordingly. Stop synthesizing calendar events from Slack DMs (they are not meetings) — Slack should only feed presence/inCall, not calendarEvent rows. Complete the calSourceMap for all providers.
verification: Create a tentative Google event spanning now; getBusyStatus.busy must be true. Send a Slack DM and confirm it does NOT flip calendar busy.

title: Every authenticated request does a Session+User DB lookup; no caching, and expired sessions are never pruned
problem: JwtStrategy.validate runs prisma.session.findUnique({ include: { user: true } }) on every request (jwt.strategy.ts:20-23). Combined with the agent/device 5s poll loops and the live-status calls, this is a constant per-request DB round-trip on the unindexed-by-userId Session table (the token lookup is indexed, but session.id PK lookup is fine; the cost is volume). Expired sessions are never deleted (logout is broken per another finding, and nothing sweeps Session where expiresAt < now), so the table grows unbounded and getSessions (users.service.ts:45-49) returns stale expired rows. There's also no check that the JWT's own exp matches session.expiresAt, but more importantly no session-revocation cache.
fix: Add a short-TTL Redis cache of validated sessions (the ioredis dep is already present), keyed by sessionId, invalidated on logout/delete. Add a periodic job (or DB TTL) to delete sessions where expiresAt < now. Index Session.userId for getSessions.
verification: Load-test an authenticated endpoint and confirm session validation hits cache (DB query count flat under load). Confirm expired Session rows are purged.

title: CORS allows any *.trycloudflare.com / *.azurestaticapps.net / *.azurewebsites.net origin with credentials
problem: enableCors uses regexes /\.trycloudflare\.com$/, /\.azurestaticapps\.net$/, /\.azurewebsites\.net$/ with credentials:true (main.ts:8-17). These are shared multi-tenant domains: any attacker can spin up a free trycloudflare tunnel or an Azure Static Web App and get a same-suffix origin, so their page is allowed to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this API and read responses. Since auth is a Bearer token (not a cookie) the immediate CSRF/credential-replay risk is reduced, but combined with the public oauth-login/demo-login endpoints this broadens the attack surface and would be dangerous if cookies are ever introduced.
fix: Pin CORS to exact known origins (the specific Static Web App hostname and the specific tunnel/prod domain) via an allowlist from config, not a wildcard suffix regex on shared domains. Drop credentials:true unless cookies are actually used.
verification: From an origin like https://evil.trycloudflare.com, a credentialed fetch to the API must be blocked by CORS; from the configured origin it succeeds.

title: live-status (5s) and battery (60s) polling never pause when tab is hidden
problem: The Messages page polls /integrations/live-status every 5s and /device/battery every 60s for the entire lifetime of the page, with no visibility gating. A user who leaves this tab open in the background keeps a 5-second request loop running indefinitely, draining laptop/phone battery and generating continuous backend load. Polling the BATTERY level frequently is especially ironic for a product whose value prop is '12-month battery'.
fix: Pause both intervals when `document.visibilityState !== 'visible'` and resume + immediately refetch on `visibilitychange`. Consider moving live-status to an EventSource/SSE stream so the server pushes changes instead of a 5s poll. At minimum wrap the fetch bodies in a visibility check.
verification: On /messages, watch the Network panel: live-status requests stop within one interval after switching to another tab and resume on return.

title: useBusyStatus evaluates busy state from refs, causing stale/missed transitions
problem: The combined-busy effect depends on [slackPresence, token, sendMessage] but reads calendarBusy.current and latestCalendar.current (refs). When the calendar poll flips calendarBusy from free->busy (or busy->free), this effect does NOT re-run because refs are not reactive and slackPresence did not change — so a calendar-driven transition is only detected on the next incidental slackPresence tick (up to 1s later, or never if Slack is not connected and presence never updates). The result is missed/late FREE/BUSY messages pushed to the device. The initial-state branch (line 111-116) also captures latestCalendar at first render, which may still be the default {busy:false} before the first poll resolves, sending a wrong initial 'FREE'.
fix: Make calendar status reactive: drive the evaluation effect off state, not refs. Add calendarStatus (the state value) to the dependency array and compute `const isBusy = slackBusy || calendarStatus.busy;` so the effect re-runs when the calendar poll updates state. Remove the calendarBusy/latestCalendar refs or keep them only as a read cache that the effect also depends on.
verification: Mock /integrations/busy to return busy=true with no Slack account connected; confirm a 'BUSY ...' message is POSTed to /messages within one calendar poll cycle (≤30s) rather than never.

title: Calendar fetch effect depends on the whole session object and recomputed dates, refetching too often
problem: The events useEffect lists [session, currentDate, view] as deps. `session` is a new object reference on many useSession() updates (e.g. focus refetch, token refresh), so the effect re-runs and refetches even when nothing relevant changed. Additionally weekStart/start/end are recomputed via date-fns on every render and used inside the effect but not memoized, and there is no AbortController, so overlapping requests from rapid navigation can resolve out of order and render stale events (data-fetching race).
fix: Depend on the token only (`const token=(session as any)?.apiToken`) plus currentDate.getTime() and view. Memoize the date range or compute it inside the effect. Add an AbortController and ignore aborted/stale responses: `const ac=new AbortController(); ...{signal:ac.signal}; return ()=>ac.abort();` Guard setState with an `if(!ignore)` flag.
verification: Rapidly click next/prev week several times; confirm only the latest range's events render (no flicker to an older range) and that the network shows no redundant refetch when the session object updates without a token change.
locationNote:
Code confirmed, but the cited path is wrong. Actual file: /Users/antoniorodes/Documents/BUMEET/platform/apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx (the finding cites src/app/(dashboard)/page.tsx, missing the platform/apps/web/ prefix). Line numbers 39-51 are exact.

Verified at lines 39-51: useEffect deps are [session, currentDate, view]. The effect already does `const token = (session as any)?.apiToken` on line 40 but still depends on the whole `session` object. useSession() returns a fresh object reference on focus refetch / token refresh / re-render, so the effect re-runs and refetches the calendar even when apiToken is unchanged — REAL over-refetching. Switching the dep to `token` is trivial and matches the proposed fix's own snippet.

Race condition is also REAL: api.get() at line 47 has no AbortController and no stale-response guard, so rapid prev/next navigation (navigate() at lines 69-73) fires overlapping requests that can resolve out of order and render stale events. Adding an `ignore` flag or AbortController is the correct, non-breaking fix.

Minor caveat on the finding's reasoning: weekStart (line 36) is recomputed every render and is used inside the effect (lines 43-44) without being a dep, which is an exhaustive-deps lint smell, but it does NOT cause extra refetches because it's deterministic from currentDate (which IS a dep). Memoizing it is cosmetic, not a correctness fix. The substantive issues (session-ref churn + missing abort/stale-guard) are both genuine. Proposed fix is safe and correct.

title: Per-send polling interval is not cleared on unmount (leak + setState on unmounted component)
problem: handleSend starts `setInterval(... 2500)` plus a 30s `setTimeout` to track delivery, but these are local to the handler and are never registered for cleanup. If the user navigates away (or sends another message) before delivery, the interval keeps firing api.get and calling setMessages on an unmounted component, leaking timers and triggering React state-update-after-unmount warnings. Multiple sends spawn multiple independent intervals with no dedupe.
fix: Track active poll timers in a useRef array and clear them in a useEffect cleanup on unmount. Inside the interval callback, bail if a mounted-ref is false. Better: replace the per-message poll with the existing 5s live-status/status stream, or use the React Query client already provided to dedupe and auto-cancel.
verification: Send a non-permanent message, immediately navigate to /status, and confirm via Network panel that GET /messages/:id polling stops and no React unmount warning appears in the console.
locationNote: Code confirmed exactly as described. Line numbers 410-417 are correct, but the cited file PATH is wrong: it omits the monorepo prefix. Actual path is /Users/antoniorodes/Documents/BUMEET/platform/apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/messages/page.tsx (not src/app/... at repo root). In handleSend, `const poll = setInterval(..., 2500)` (line 411) and `setTimeout(() => clearInterval(poll), 30000)` (line 416) are local to the async handler closure and never registered for cleanup. The component's only useEffect (lines 379-396) cleans up its own battInterval/statusInterval but has no knowledge of these per-send timers. On unmount while a poll is active, the interval keeps calling api.get + setMessages on an unmounted component (state-update-after-unmount warning) and leaks the timer; the 30s timeout also leaks. Multiple sends within 30s spawn multiple independent untracked intervals with no dedupe. Genuine medium-severity bug, not already handled, not a false positive. Proposed fix (track timers in a useRef array, clear in a useEffect cleanup, add a mounted-ref guard inside the callback) is safe, non-breaking, and correct; the suggested alternatives (reuse the existing 5s live-status poll, or React Query dedupe) are also valid but larger refactors.

title: <html lang="en"> but the landing/metadata/cookie banner content is Spanish
problem: The root layout hardcodes lang="en", yet the metadata (layout.tsx:7-13), the cookie banner (CookieBanner.tsx:45-50) and the default landing copy (corporate/page.tsx:1026 defaults to 'es') are Spanish. Screen readers will use the wrong pronunciation/voice, and it hurts SEO and translation tooling. The landing also toggles language client-side without updating the document lang at all.
fix: Set the document language to match the primary content (e.g. `<html lang="es">` since locale is es_ES and copy defaults to Spanish), and when the landing language toggle changes, update `document.documentElement.lang`. For a fully correct fix, drive lang from the active locale.
verification: Load the site, inspect <html>; confirm lang matches the rendered language, and that toggling EN/ES on the landing updates document.documentElement.lang.

Line 22 is correct: `<html lang="en">`. All supporting claims verified: metadata is Spanish with locale 'es_ES' (layout.tsx:6-18); CookieBanner is Spanish ("Usamos cookies necesarias...", CookieBanner.tsx:45-58); corporate/page.tsx defaults to Spanish via `useState<Lang>('es')` (actual line 1030, near cited 1026). The landing language toggle (setLang at corporate/page.tsx:309,342) only updates React context — it never mutates document.documentElement.lang, so the document lang stays 'en' regardless of selected language. This is a genuine a11y (wrong screen-reader pronunciation) and SEO/i18n issue, not already handled. Proposed fix is safe: changing to lang="es" matches the es_ES locale and default content; syncing document.documentElement.lang on toggle (e.g. via useEffect on the active lang in LandingPage, or driving lang from locale) is the standard correct approach and non-breaking. title: Permanent-message toggle is a div with onClick — not keyboard or screen-reader operable
problem: The 'Keep on display permanently' switch is a <div onClick> inside a <label>, with no role, no tabindex, no aria-checked, and no keyboard handler. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users cannot perceive it as a switch or toggle it (the label wraps a non-form control, so clicking the label text does nothing either). This is a WCAG 2.1 keyboard/name-role-value failure on a control that changes message behavior.
fix: Use a real control: `<button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked={permanent} aria-label="Keep on display permanently" onClick={()=>setPermanent(p=>!p)}>` (or an `<input type="checkbox" className="sr-only">` visually styled as the track/thumb). Native button/checkbox gives focusability, Space/Enter activation, and correct semantics for free.
verification: Tab to the toggle, press Space to flip it, and confirm a screen reader announces 'switch, on/off'. Run axe DevTools on /messages with no new violations on this control.

title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts, defeating XSS protection
problem: The Content-Security-Policy uses `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`. 'unsafe-inline' permits arbitrary inline <script> and event-handler injection, which neutralizes CSP's primary value as an XSS mitigation — exactly the threat that matters given a bearer token is exposed to client JS (see security-apitoken-exposed-to-client). connect-src is also pinned to https://api.bumeet.es while NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL could differ, potentially breaking fetches or forcing a looser policy later.
fix: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src and adopt a nonce or hash-based policy for the few inline scripts Next emits (Next supports CSP nonces). If a strict nonce policy is too large a change immediately, at minimum prioritize it as hardening. Verify connect-src includes the actual API origin used at runtime.
verification: Load the app, open the console, and confirm no CSP violations after removing 'unsafe-inline'; verify auth and API calls still function and that an injected ``/inline script is blocked.
locationNote:
CONFIRMED REAL. The CSP at line 8 contains `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` exactly as described, plus the same for style-src. 'unsafe-inline' on script-src does neutralize CSP's XSS-mitigation value, which is the core claim and it is accurate.

FILE/LINE CORRECTION: The cited path is wrong. The correct path is /Users/antoniorodes/Documents/BUMEET/platform/apps/web/staticwebapp.config.json (not the repo-root staticwebapp.config.json, which does not exist). The line number (8) is correct within that file. Full directive: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://api.bumeet.es; frame-ancestors 'none'".

NOT ALREADY MITIGATED: No app-authored nonce/hash CSP exists. The only `nonce` references in the codebase are inside Next.js's own compiled framework chunks (.next/server/...), not custom CSP handling. No CSP middleware present.

connect-src NOTE: Valid concern. NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is http://localhost:3001/api/v1 locally (src/lib/api.ts, src/lib/auth.ts, .env.local) while connect-src pins https://api.bumeet.es. In prod the SWA presumably serves api.bumeet.es so it works, and 'self' covers same-origin, so it is not currently broken — but the brittleness observation is fair.

FIX SAFETY/CORRECTNESS: The fix direction (remove 'unsafe-inline', adopt nonce/hash) is the correct, standard hardening. One important caveat the verifier should weigh: Azure Static Web Apps' staticwebapp.config.json serves STATIC headers and cannot inject per-request nonces, so a strict nonce policy requires moving CSP generation into Next.js middleware/runtime, not editing this JSON file. The finding's own hedge ("if a strict nonce policy is too large a change immediately, at minimum prioritize it as hardening") correctly acknowledges this. So the fix is safe and non-breaking but is a non-trivial refactor, not a one-line edit. Severity medium is appropriate (note style-src 'unsafe-inline' is also present but is a lower priority and not flagged).

It also console.logs the submitter's name, email and message excerpt (line 17), writing PII to server/host logs with no consent or retention control, and there is no validation/anti-spam (any payload with three non-empty fields is accepted, enabling log/email spam).

verification: Submit the contact form; confirm an email is actually received and that a forced transport failure returns a non-200 the UI surfaces. Grep server logs to confirm no raw email/message is written.

title: Public anonymous-read storage serving executables with no CDN, integrity, or access logging
problem: releases_storage allows anonymous public blob read (allow_nested_items_to_be_public=true, container access_type='blob', lines 13,29) and serves unsigned executables (bumeet-agent-macos/linux, .exe) straight from *.blob.core.windows.net (outputs.tf:7). There is no Front Door/CDN in front (so egress is billed at full blob rates and there's no WAF/rate limiting), no diagnostic logging of downloads, no checksum/SHA publication for integrity, and the storage account uses LRS only (main.tf:10) so a single-region failure loses the download endpoint. The connection string is also surfaced as a root output (outputs.tf:46-50) and stored in state.
fix: Front the container with Azure Front Door/CDN and point download URLs at the CDN endpoint (better caching, TLS, WAF, lower egress). Publish SHA256SUMS alongside binaries and have installers verify them. Enable storage diagnostic logging to Log Analytics. Consider disabling anonymous access and issuing short-lived SAS or using Front Door with private origin. Add Windows signing (only macOS signing exists in agent-release.yml).
verification: Download URL resolves via the CDN/Front Door hostname; az storage account show --query allowBlobPublicAccess reviewed; a SHA256SUMS file is published and verified by install scripts.

title: Prod Postgres GP_Standard_D2s_v3 + 64GB likely over-provisioned for a small app
problem: Prod provisions GP_Standard_D2s_v3 (2 vCPU / 8 GB General Purpose) with 65536 MB storage (envs/prod/main.tf:10-11). For a small NestJS app this is a meaningful monthly spend (GP tier is several times the Burstable cost) and the choice appears default-driven rather than sized from real load. There is no storage auto-grow, and no evidence of connection-pool sizing to justify GP. Meanwhile dev correctly uses B1ms Burstable. If actual prod load is light, B2ms/B2s Burstable or a smaller GP would cut cost substantially.
fix: Right-size from observed metrics once App Insights/diagnostics exist: start prod at the smallest GP that meets connection/CPU needs, or B-series Burstable if load is genuinely low and you don't need the GP SLA. Enable storage auto-grow (auto_grow_enabled=true) instead of pre-provisioning 64 GB. Re-evaluate after the HA decision (HA requires GP/MO).
verification: az monitor metrics list for cpu_percent / memory_percent / active_connections over a representative week shows headroom; resize via terraform and confirm no throttling.

title: Dev Redis Basic C0 cannot be stopped and bills 24/7 despite nightly shutdown; Redis necessity unjustified
problem: The stop workflow explicitly notes Redis 'Always on (Basic C0, cannot stop)' (line 64), so while App Service and Postgres are stopped nightly to save cost, the Basic C0 cache bills continuously — the cost-savings story is incomplete. More fundamentally, there is no evidence Redis is actually required: a small app often uses it only for session/cache and could rely on in-memory or a managed alternative. Basic C0 also has no SLA and no replica, so even in dev it's a paid resource that may be unnecessary. If Redis is needed only for prod (e.g. BullMQ/queues), dev could drop it entirely.
fix: Confirm what consumes Redis (search the API for ioredis/cache-manager/bullmq usage). If dev doesn't need it, gate the redis module behind a count/var so dev provisions none. If needed only intermittently in dev, accept the small C0 cost but document it. For prod, validate Standard C1 sizing against actual memory/eviction metrics.
verification: Grep the api app for redis client usage to confirm necessity; terraform plan dev shows redis module count=0 when disabled; prod Redis used_memory/evicted_keys metrics justify C1.

title: Postgres geo-redundant backup disabled in prod; 7-day retention only; no geo-restore for DR
problem: geo_redundant_backup_enabled is hardcoded false for every env (main.tf:11) and backup_retention_days is hardcoded 7 (main.tf:12), so prod has no cross-region backup and only a 7-day recovery window. A regional outage or a data-corruption discovered after a week is unrecoverable, which contradicts the prod sla=99.9 tag and any reasonable RPO/RTO. These values are not parameterized per environment.
fix: Parameterize backups: for prod set geo_redundant_backup_enabled=true and backup_retention_days to 14-35. Keep dev at false/7 for cost. Document the resulting RPO/RTO and test a point-in-time restore.
verification: terraform plan prod shows geo_redundant_backup_enabled true and retention >=14; az postgres flexible-server show --query backup confirms; a test PITR restore succeeds.

title: Single shared releases storage account is created by BOTH dev and prod root invocations into different RGs
problem: releases_storage uses a globally-unique fixed name 'stbumeetreleases' (main.tf:86) but is declared in the shared root module, so it is created once into rg-bumeet-dev (when env=dev) and again into rg-bumeet-prod (when env=prod). Because the storage account name is globally unique, the second environment's apply will fail with a name-conflict, or the resource will ping-pong ownership between the two state files (each apply trying to manage the same physical account from a different RG). The comment says 'one shared storage account across environments' but the code has no guard (count/env check) to provision it in only one env.
fix: Provision the releases storage account in exactly one place — either move it to the bootstrap module (which is env-agnostic) or gate it with count = var.env == "prod" ? 1 : 0 and import it into a single state. Reference its outputs from the other env via data source or remote state rather than re-declaring.
verification: terraform apply for both dev and prod succeeds with no 'StorageAccountAlreadyTaken' error; only one state file has the storage account in its resources.

title: Key Vault uses legacy access policies (incl. Purge for CI) instead of RBAC least-privilege; no network ACL
problem: The vault uses the legacy access_policy model (main.tf:13-18) granting the CI/Terraform principal Get/List/Set/Delete/Purge on secrets, and a second policy in root main.tf:169-177 grants the App Service identity Get/List. enable_rbac_authorization is not set, so RBAC's finer-grained, auditable role assignments aren't used, and the CI principal holds destructive Delete+Purge permanently (compounding the purge-protection finding). There is also no network ACL on the vault (no network_acls block / public access restricted), so the vault endpoint is publicly reachable.
fix: Set enable_rbac_authorization = true and replace access policies with role assignments: 'Key Vault Secrets Officer' for the CI principal (or 'Key Vault Secrets User' if CI shouldn't write), and 'Key Vault Secrets User' for the App Service identity. Remove Purge/Delete from CI. Add network_acls { default_action = "Deny" } with the App Service subnet / Front Door and CI ranges allowed, plus a private endpoint for prod.
verification: az keyvault show --query properties.enableRbacAuthorization true; role assignments show Secrets User on the app identity; CI cannot purge; vault network default action Deny.

title: Production web deploy fires on every push to main with no environment approval and no preceding quality gate
problem: web-deploy-prod.yml deploys straight to the production Static Web App on every push to main touching the web app (lines 6-12) with no `environment:` approval gate and no `needs:` dependency on the Quality workflow. quality.yml only runs on pull_request (line 4-5), so a push merged without the PR checks completing (or a direct push to main) ships unverified code to production. Both web-deploy.yml (dev, also on push to main) and web-deploy-prod.yml run on the same trigger, so a single merge simultaneously updates dev and prod with no promotion step.
fix: Gate prod web deploy behind a protected GitHub `prod` environment requiring manual approval, and/or make it `needs` a green build/test job. Separate dev (auto) from prod (approved promotion of the same build artifact). Add branch protection requiring the quality status check on main.
verification: A push to main pauses at the prod environment approval before deploying; the prod deploy reuses the artifact validated in CI; direct-to-prod without checks is blocked by branch protection.

title: Third-party GitHub Actions referenced by mutable tags, not pinned to commit SHA
problem: Across the workflows, actions are referenced by mutable major-version tags (e.g. docker/build-push-action@v5, azure/webapps-deploy@v3, azure/login@v2, softprops/action-gh-release@v2, Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1, actions/github-script@v7). A compromised or retagged third-party action would run with the workflow's credentials — and several of these jobs hold AZURE_CREDENTIALS, ARM secrets, deployment tokens, signing certs (agent-release.yml), and contents:write (agent-release.yml:156). Tag references can be moved by the maintainer or an attacker who gains push access to that action's repo.
fix: Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA (with a comment noting the version), and let Dependabot (already configured for github-actions) bump the SHAs. SHA-pinning is the robust default for supply-chain safety.
verification: All `uses:` lines reference 40-char SHAs; Dependabot opens PRs updating the SHAs; a moved upstream tag no longer changes CI behavior.

title: Core2 allocates WriteCallback with new (heap) vs CoreInk's static instance
problem: pChar->setCallbacks(new WriteCallback()) heap-allocates the callback and never deletes it. It is created once in setup() so it is not a growing leak, but it is inconsistent with CoreInk which uses a static gWriteCb instance (line 211, 250) and avoids the allocation entirely. Heap allocation here is unnecessary and slightly fragments the heap at boot.
fix: Use a static instance like CoreInk: declare `static WriteCallback gWriteCb;` at file scope and call pChar->setCallbacks(&gWriteCb);
verification: Compile and confirm behavior unchanged; ESP.getFreeHeap() after setup should be marginally higher.

title: Core2 has no disconnect/auto-FREE handling — stale BUSY persists indefinitely when agent leaves
problem: Core2 has no onDisconnect handling and no auto-FREE timeout (CoreInk clears to FREE after 5 min without a connection, lines 55, 371-379). If the desktop agent goes out of range or the laptop sleeps while the device shows BUSY, the Core2 will display a stale BUSY forever until the agent reconnects and writes again. For a presence indicator on a door, this shows the wrong status to colleagues.
fix: Add ServerCallbacks tracking connection state and a disconnect timestamp; in the loop, if disconnected for > AUTO_FREE_TIMEOUT and gCurrentMsg != FREE, render FREE. Mirror the CoreInk logic.
verification: Show BUSY, disconnect the agent, wait past the timeout, and confirm the LCD falls back to FREE.

title: Long ulTaskNotifyTake waits (up to 60 s) with no explicit task watchdog feed
problem: The loop blocks in ulTaskNotifyTake for up to TASK_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 ms (and the disconnected/auto-FREE branches can compute large remaining waits clamped to 60 s). The Arduino loopTask on ESP32 normally has the task watchdog disabled, so this is usually fine, but if the build enables CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK or the loop WDT, a 60 s block plus light sleep can trip the watchdog and reset the device. There is no esp_task_wdt_reset()/feed anywhere. Relying on the default WDT-off configuration is fragile across Arduino-ESP32 core versions.
fix: Either explicitly disable the loop task WDT for this task (esp_task_wdt_delete(NULL)) in setup, or cap the blocking wait and feed the WDT each wake. Document the assumption that the loop WDT is off.
verification: Build with the loop task WDT enabled and confirm the device does not reset during a 60 s idle block; or confirm esp_task_wdt is not registered for the loop task.

title: New aiohttp ClientSession created per one-shot request in config fetch — avoidable TLS/connector churn
problem: `_fetch_remote_ble_config` (line 45) opens a fresh `aiohttp.ClientSession` for a single GET, doing a full TLS handshake/connector setup. The main `_api_poll_loop` correctly reuses one session (service.py:108) and the pairing status poll reuses one in its loop (app.py:111), so this is the one-shot path. Minor versus detection/BLE issues but avoidable network/CPU cost.
fix: Share a single ClientSession across config fetch, pairing, and live-status poll (e.g. on the container), closing it at shutdown.
verification: Confirm one session/connector is reused across config+pairing+poll; no functional change.

title: SettingsStore.load crashes on corrupt config JSON; save is non-atomic and can corrupt the token file
problem: `load()` does `json.loads(read_text())` then `model_validate(...)` with no try/except (lines 88-89). A truncated/corrupt config.json (e.g. from a crash mid-`write_text`, which is non-atomic at line 94) or a schema change raises JSONDecodeError/ValidationError at startup before the orchestrator, so the agent fails to launch with a raw traceback and the user is stuck. The non-atomic save (truncate-then-write at line 94) can corrupt the only copy of the (plaintext) token+config on crash.
fix: Wrap load() in try/except: log a warning, back up the bad file, return `AppSettings()` (re-trigger pairing) instead of crashing. Make save() atomic: write to a temp file in the same dir then `os.replace`. Apply restrictive permissions (see token-plaintext-config).
verification: Write a malformed config.json and start the agent; assert it logs a warning and proceeds (re-pairs). Kill the process mid-save and confirm the existing config isn't truncated.

title: Uses asyncio.get_event_loop().time() (deprecated pattern) for pairing TTL and BLE timing
problem: `_pair_with_portal` computes the 5-minute deadline with `asyncio.get_event_loop().time()` (lines 110, 112). `get_event_loop()` inside a coroutine is discouraged in favor of `get_running_loop()`. ble/client.py uses the same pattern at lines 80, 94, 102, 112, 217. Functionally monotonic time is fine for intervals, but the deprecated accessor should be replaced and the pairing TTL should defer to the server's authoritative 'expired' status (already honored at app.py:134) rather than the local monotonic deadline, which can diverge across system suspend.
fix: Replace with `asyncio.get_running_loop().time()` (or `time.monotonic()`). Keep relying on the server's `expired` status for the authoritative pairing expiry.
verification: Static: grep for get_event_loop and replace; tests pass with no behavior change.

title: Simulation viewer rebuilds the entire Text widget on every log line — O(n^2) over a run
problem: `_append_log` reads the full current Text contents, concatenates, and `_set_log_contents` deletes 1.0..END and re-inserts everything (lines 219-229). For every event this is O(current_log_length), so a long simulation does O(n^2) total work and visibly lags as the log grows; the 100ms `after` poll (line 195) compounds it. Dev tooling, so low severity, but long scenarios get sluggish.
fix: Append only the new line (state normal, insert at END, see END, state disabled) instead of rebuilding from the full string; cap retained lines.
verification: Run a long/looping scenario and confirm the UI stays responsive and CPU stays flat as the log grows.

title: Keepalive/reconnect writes hardcode response=False while real writes honor settings.write_with_response
problem: The reconnect-sync write (line 92) and keepalive write (line 110) hardcode `response=False`, but `send_payload` honors `self._settings.write_with_response` (default True, line 215). If the firmware/characteristic requires acknowledged writes, the keepalive and post-reconnect resync use unacknowledged writes that can be silently dropped under congestion — they 'succeed' locally (no exception, `_last_write_time` updated) without the firmware receiving them, so macOS may still drop the idle link and the display may not resync after reconnect.
fix: Use `response=self._settings.write_with_response` for the keepalive and reconnect-sync writes (at least make the post-reconnect resync acknowledged), or document why fire-and-forget is intentional.
verification: On hardware requiring acknowledged writes, confirm the display resyncs after a forced disconnect and the idle link survives past 45s with keepalives delivered.

title: No security headers (helmet), no payload size limit, validation pipe does not forbid non-whitelisted props
problem: bootstrap() sets CORS and a ValidationPipe but adds no helmet/security headers, no global body size limit, and forbidNonWhitelisted:false (main.ts:25) so unexpected properties are silently dropped rather than rejected. The OAuth callbacks redirect to FRONTEND_URL-derived URLs with attacker-influenced query (?error=, ?connected=) which is fine, but the missing headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame options) and absent JSON body limit leave the API more exposed than necessary. ValidationPipe is also not configured to reject on unknown fields, weakening input strictness on the inline DTOs.
fix: Add app.use(helmet()), set an express json limit (e.g. app.use(express.json({ limit: '100kb' }))), and set ValidationPipe forbidNonWhitelisted:true so malformed/extra fields are rejected. Add a ConfigModule Joi validationSchema to assert required env vars at boot.
verification: Inspect response headers for helmet defaults; POST an oversized body and confirm 413; POST a DTO with an extra field and confirm 400.

title: getBattery treats a real 0% battery as 'no data' due to falsy check
problem: getBattery returns null when !user?.batteryLevel (device.service.ts:33). batteryLevel is a valid Int that can legitimately be 0 (dead/critical battery), but 0 is falsy, so a device reporting 0% is reported as 'no battery data' to the UI (device.controller.ts:41 then returns { level: null }). The most safety-relevant battery state (empty) is silently hidden.
fix: Check for null/undefined explicitly: if (user?.batteryLevel == null || !user.batteryUpdatedAt) return null; so that 0 is preserved.
verification: PATCH /device/battery {level:0} then GET /device/battery; expect { level: 0, ... }, not { level: null }.

title: Pairing status endpoint is unauthenticated with weak validation and the approve/register regexes are inconsistent
problem: GET /agent/pair/status takes a raw ?code query with only a length===6 check (pairing.controller.ts:33-34, no charset/format validation) and is unauthenticated, returning the agent token to whoever polls a valid approved code. The codes are 6 chars from a 27-symbol alphabet (~27^6 ≈ 3.9e8) with a 5-min TTL and no per-IP rate limit (Throttler is not enforced — see other finding), so they are brute-forceable, especially since poll() consumes the token to the FIRST caller that polls after approval (pairing.service.ts:61-64). RegisterDto allows [A-Z0-9] (pairing.controller.ts:9) while ApproveDto allows [A-Za-z0-9] (line 17) and the generator only emits a 27-char subset — inconsistent, and digits 0/1 in the regex are not in the generator alphabet.
fix: Require the agent to authenticate the status poll with a per-pairing nonce issued at register time (return a random pollSecret from register, require it on status), bind approval to that secret, and rate-limit the status endpoint hard. Lengthen the code or shorten TTL. Make the register/approve/poll charset validation consistent with the actual ALPHABET.
verification: Brute-forcing /agent/pair/status with random codes must be rate-limited and cannot retrieve a token without the pollSecret; a race where a second poller steals the token is prevented.

title: disconnect deletes events then integration in two statements without a transaction (cascade already covers it)
problem: disconnect runs deleteMany(calendarEvent) then delete(integrationAccount) as two separate awaits (integrations.service.ts:338-339). The schema already has onDelete: Cascade from CalendarEvent -> IntegrationAccount (schema.prisma:84), so the first deleteMany is redundant; more importantly the two ops aren't in a transaction, so a crash between them leaves orphaned state (here harmless due to cascade, but the pattern is fragile and the manual delete masks the cascade). Same non-transactional read-then-write ownership pattern appears in triggerSync and the upserts.
fix: Drop the redundant deleteMany and rely on the cascade, or wrap both in prisma.$transaction([...]). Generally wrap multi-statement mutations in $transaction for atomicity.
verification: Disconnect an integration; confirm its CalendarEvent rows are gone (via cascade) and the operation is atomic.

title: ioredis is a declared dependency but Redis is never used — no caching, no distributed locks, no queues
problem: package.json declares ioredis (line 27) and .env defines REDIS_URL, but there is zero Redis usage in src (grep confirms). The codebase has multiple places that specifically need Redis and reimplement worse alternatives in-process: OAuth state storage, presence caching, session validation caching, the distributed sync-loop lock, the durable message-delivery timers, and the in-memory pairing store (pairing.service.ts:18, which is lost on restart and not shared across instances). This is dead infrastructure dependency plus missed performance wins.
fix: Either remove the unused dependency/env, or (preferably) wire Redis in for: per-instance-safe sync scheduling lock, presence/live-status cache, session cache, OAuth state, and a durable job queue (BullMQ) replacing setTimeout-based message transitions and the in-memory pairing map.
verification: Either grep shows ioredis is actually imported and used, or it is removed from package.json and .env.

title: changePassword DTO has no minimum length and password change does not revoke other sessions
problem: ChangePasswordDto.newPassword is just @IsString() with no @MinLength (update-user.dto.ts:25), unlike RegisterDto which enforces MinLength(8). So a user can set a 1-char password. Additionally, UsersService.changePassword (users.service.ts:27-37) updates the hash but does NOT delete other Session rows, so if an account was compromised, changing the password does not log the attacker out — their 7-day token/session keeps working. deleteAccount (users.service.ts:39-42) relies on cascade (fine) but also doesn't revoke the JWT.
fix: Add @MinLength(8) (and ideally complexity) to newPassword. On password change, prisma.session.deleteMany({ where: { userId, NOT: { id: currentSessionId } } }) to revoke all other sessions. Track currentSessionId via the strategy fix.
verification: Change password and confirm a previously issued token from a different session is rejected; confirm a 3-char new password is rejected with 400.

title: POST /agent/presence authenticates and validates but discards the input — does nothing
problem: updatePresence resolves the user from the agent key then returns { status, updatedAt } without persisting anything (agent.controller.ts:26-30). It never updates User.micActive/micUpdatedAt (the fields the live-status engine actually reads at integrations.service.ts:95-98). The real mic update path is the JWT-guarded PATCH /device/presence (device.controller.ts:44-47). So an agent that posts to /agent/presence believes it reported busy/free but the signal is silently dropped, and the endpoint exists as misleading dead code.
fix: Either remove the endpoint, or have it write micActive (map 'busy'->true, 'free'->false) to the resolved user via DeviceService.updatePresence so the agent token path actually feeds presence. Align the agent's reporting path with the live-status reader fields.

title: Many always-on animate-pulse indicators keep compositing/repainting continuously

title: Query-param banner effect omits router from deps and re-runs only on searchParams
problem: The effect reading ?connected/?error calls router.replace inside but lists only [searchParams] as deps (router omitted — an exhaustive-deps lint violation). More importantly, router.replace('/integrations') changes the URL but the effect can re-fire on the resulting searchParams change; because banner is also a dependency of the load effect (line 68), this couples URL cleanup, banner state, and data reload in a fragile way. On Azure SWA static hosting, router.replace to a clean path can also momentarily mismatch the SWA fallback if config regresses.
fix: Add router to the dependency array (or disable the lint rule intentionally with a comment), and guard so the effect only acts when a param is actually present. Decouple the integrations reload from `banner` by reloading explicitly after a successful connect instead of using banner as a dependency.
verification: Complete an OAuth connect redirect back with ?connected=slack; confirm the success banner shows once, the URL cleans to /integrations, and the list reloads exactly once (no double fetch) via the Network panel.

The effect reads ?connected/?error, calls router.replace('/integrations') inside, but lists only [searchParams] as deps — router is omitted. The load effect at line 68 does depend on banner ([token, banner]), so the connect flow couples URL cleanup -> banner state -> data reload, which is fragile as described. Proposed fix (add router to deps or add an intentional eslint-disable comment, and decouple the reload from banner by reloading explicitly after a successful connect) is safe and non-breaking. Recommend keeping it as a low-priority cleanup.

title: No CDN/Front Door fronting the API; single origin directly exposed
problem: The Static Web App has Microsoft's edge built in, but the NestJS API (api.bumeet.es) is served directly from a single App Service instance with no Azure Front Door / CDN in front. That means no global edge TLS termination, no WAF, no caching of cacheable GETs, no edge-level rate limiting/DDoS shaping, and no health-probe-based failover. For an API consumed by a web app and desktop agents this raises latency for distant clients and leaves the origin directly exposed.
fix: Optionally place Azure Front Door (Standard) in front of the App Service with a WAF policy, health probes, and caching rules for cacheable endpoints; restrict the App Service to accept traffic only from Front Door (access restriction by X-Azure-FDID / service tag). This also gives a single WAF-protected ingress for both SWA and API.
verification: API resolves via the Front Door hostname; App Service access restrictions reject direct origin hits lacking the Front Door header; WAF logs show requests.

The App Service already sets https_only=true (line 16), http2_enabled=true, and a health_check_path=/api/v1/health (line 30), so basic TLS and instance health are covered — just not at a global edge with WAF. The proposed fix (Azure Front Door Standard + WAF policy + health probes + caching + restricting App Service ingress to Front Door via X-Azure-FDID / AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag) is safe, correct, and additive (non-breaking) — the only caveat is the access-restriction lock-down must be applied AFTER Front Door is wired up to avoid locking out the origin, and direct *.azurewebsites.net access should be blocked once FDID validation is in place. title: Gitleaks push scan only inspects the last commit and pins the latest release at runtime
problem: On push, gitleaks scans only `--log-opts=-1` (HEAD only, line 41), so a secret introduced in any commit other than the tip of a multi-commit push (or pushed directly bypassing PRs) is not detected. The installer also resolves 'releases/latest' at runtime (lines 20-24) and curls an unpinned binary, so the security scanner itself is a supply-chain risk (an unexpected upstream change or a compromised release alters CI behavior). PR scans use base..HEAD which is fine, but the push path is the gap.
fix: On push, scan the full push range (github.event.before..github.sha) or run gitleaks over the whole history periodically. Pin gitleaks to a specific version and verify its checksum, or use the official gitleaks-action pinned by SHA. Fail closed if the install step can't verify the binary.
verification: Introduce a fake secret in a non-tip commit of a multi-commit push; the push scan fails. Gitleaks version is pinned and checksum-verified in logs.

title: No scheduled drift detection and no state-lock timeout; out-of-band CI image deploys guarantee silent drift
problem: The azurerm backend (prod/backend.tf, dev/backend.tf) supports blob-lease locking, but apply runs never set -lock-timeout, so a stale lease (from a cancelled run) hard-fails deploys. There is no scheduled `terraform plan` drift-detection workflow, so drift introduced by out-of-band changes — notably azure/webapps-deploy setting the container image on every API deploy against a module that declares a Node stack (see app-service-node-stack-vs-docker-deploy) and the manual az start/stop of dev resources — accumulates undetected until someone runs apply and gets a surprising diff.
fix: Add -lock-timeout=5m to plan/apply. Add a scheduled (e.g. nightly) drift-detection job running `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` per env and alerting on exit code 2. Use lifecycle ignore_changes for attributes legitimately managed out-of-band (container image; pg zone already handled).
verification: A scheduled drift job exists and reports clean after a CI deploy; a stale lock no longer permanently blocks apply due to lock-timeout.

title: Dev App Service always_on=false on B1 causes cold starts and unloads background timers
problem: Dev sets api_always_on=false (envs/dev/main.tf:8, default variables.tf:39). On Basic B1 with always_on disabled, the worker is unloaded after ~20 minutes of inactivity, causing cold-start latency on the first request and — critically — stopping any in-process background work (this is exactly why the Prisma keepalive timer never fires in dev). It also makes the health_check_path (/api/v1/health) probe meaningless while the app is unloaded.
fix: If dev needs to stay responsive during work hours, set always_on=true (B1 supports it) and rely on the nightly stop workflow for cost control; or accept cold starts as the intended cost tradeoff and remove any code that assumes a persistent background loop. Make the choice explicit and consistent with the keepalive decision.
verification: az webapp config show --query alwaysOn matches intent; first-request latency after idle is acceptable; no background-timer code depends on the worker staying loaded.

title: Uses deprecated enable_https_traffic_only argument (removed in azurerm 4.x)
problem: releases_storage/main.tf:16 uses `enable_https_traffic_only = true`. This argument is deprecated in azurerm 3.x and removed/renamed to `https_traffic_only_enabled` in azurerm 4.x. The provider is pinned ~> 3.110 (versions.tf:7), so it works today, but Dependabot is configured to bump the terraform provider (dependabot.yml:41-46); a major-version bump to 4.x will break plan/apply. The bootstrap storage account (bootstrap/main.tf) does not set this at all, an inconsistency.
fix: When moving to azurerm 4.x, rename to https_traffic_only_enabled (TLS-only is the 4.x default anyway). Keep the provider major version pinned deliberately and treat the provider Dependabot PR as a breaking change requiring code updates. Align bootstrap and module storage settings.
verification: terraform validate passes under the targeted provider version; a dry-run with azurerm 4.x shows no 'unsupported argument' error.
